text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's public roads' administration (DGDP) has withdrawn from half of a road construction contract previously awarded to German Teerbau GmbH due to delays in the construction of the new A-4 Krakow-Katowice motorway.
The work will be carried out by Dromex construction firm.
- Poland's Transport Minister Boguslaw Liberadzki is ready to accept a road tax in fuel prices which would lead to a price rise by 0.11 zloty per litre.

- Irish firms are likely to participate in joint ventures with Polish companies in areas such as agriculture, transport, printing and industry, Irish business representatives said on a visit to Poznan, western Poland.
- Pepsico has bought Polish farming products worth $125 million. Most raw materials used to make Pepsico products sold in this country are Polish made, company representatives said.

- Szczecin province will sell the Goleniow-based tin packaging factory to CarnaudMetalbox Polska Ltd for over 20 million zlotys, with CarnaudMetalbox agreeing to invest 10 million zlotys for product quality improvement in the next two years.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's Labour Minister Andrzej Baczkowski wants to cover the 1.5 million zlotys needed for old age pension indexation from the privatisation of the KGHM copper combine.
- A large, professional agricultural commodity market centre will be set up in two years time in the town of Bronisze on the outskirts of Warsaw.
Similar commodity markets will be formed around the cities of Katowice, Gdansk, Lublin, Elblag, and Poznan.
- Over 200 motor industry firms are exhibiting their products at the "Autosalon'96" automotive fair, in Katowice, southern Poland.

- Infrastructural modernisation underway on the Polish-Slovak border-crossing at Chyzne-Trstena will facilitate heavy-load TIR trucks customs clearance and transit, Nowy Sacz province infrastructure director Adam Czerwinski said.
- Creditanstalt Securities will coordinate National Investment Fund (NFI) No 2's share listing operation on the Warsaw bourse.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Gdansk municipality has contracted the Budimex construction firm to build a biological sewage treatment section of the Gdansk Wschod treatment complex which will cost the city 188 million zlotys.
- The listed Elektrim industrial trade and trade conglomerate will acquire a 75-percent stake in the Cieszyn-based Celma electric maichinery plant, Elektrim president Andrzej Skowronski said.
- Nafta Polska petrochemical holding will produce a privatisation and share-subscription programme for its refineries by the end of the year, Nafta Polska representatives said.
- Poland's government has introduced duty-free petrol and diesel fuel import quotas while lowering the excise tax on diesel fuel and allowing its distributors to raise prices by 4.9 percent.
PARKIET

- The KGHM copper combine, TPSA telecom monopolist, and Wasaw-based Bank Handlowy bank will become the flagships of the Warsaw bourse once they are listed, exchange president Wieslaw Rozlucki said at the Second Capital Investments Forum yesterday.
